outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed evaluation is not discordant: both parallel and serial failed with 34/149 passed tests. The concrete process difference is that serial fixed a negative/hyphen CLI edge case in its single verification loop, while the parallel child found the negative-value mismatch but was interrupted before returning it and the parent finalized without it. Parallel also had a child/parent shared-output collision that serial avoided. These differences explain task-solution differences, but not a pass/fail split.
parallel_contributors: Child verifier finding for negative numeric argv values remained below the parent and was not fixed before final delivery.
Child and parent both wrote overlapping /output deliverable/source files, forcing late cleanup and loss of the child implementation path.
serial_contributors: Serial found that negative numeric values and markdown values starting with hyphen should be accepted, patched the parser, and verified the fixed behavior.
Serial retained a single final implementation tree without cross-agent provenance conflicts.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs hand-coded partial markdown behavior and still failed most hidden official cases.
The official summaries do not expose the exact hidden failing samples, so broader markdown gaps remain ordinary implementation limitations rather than taxonomy labels.
evaluator_effects: No evaluator anomaly is visible; only aggregate official pass counts are available in the pair.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
